lemmas.informal_hint: In an extensive category every morphism into the initial object 0 is an isomorphism. Consequently, if an object X admits a morphism X → 0, then X is initial. This is a standard consequence of extensivity, which we take as known.

lemmas.signature: ∀ {P Q X} (x : X ⇒ P) (y : X ⇒ Q) → i₁ ∘ x ≈ i₂ ∘ y → X ≅ ⊥
lemmas.informal_hint: Let P and Q be objects. The pullback of i1 : P → P + Q along i2 : Q → P + Q is initial. Consequently, if x : X → P and y : X → Q satisfy i1 ∘ x = i2 ∘ y, then X is initial. To see this, the pair (x, y) is a cone over the cospan i1, i2, so it factors through the pullback, which gives a morphism X → 0. By initialStrict, X is initial.

lemmas.name: initialCoproduct
lemmas.informal_hint: Let Z be an initial object and Y any object. Then the injection j1 : Y → Y + Z is an isomorphism. Let !_Z : Z → Y be the unique morphism, and let k = [1_Y, !_Z] : Y + Z → Y. Then k ∘ j1 = 1_Y. Also (j1 ∘ k) ∘ j1 = j1, because k ∘ j1 = 1_Y. Further, j1 ∘ k ∘ j2 and j2 are both morphisms out of the initial object Z, so they are equal. Hence j1 ∘ k agrees with the identity on both injections, and by the universal property of the coproduct j1 ∘ k = 1_{Y+Z}. So j1 is an isomorphism with inverse k.
